newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 28.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) say the government should forget about a surplus budget next year. The Czech-Moravian federation of labour unions has a similar opinion, but Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus rejects this measure and believes that flood damages can be covered by small privatisations and bonds.
- From today until August 4, Czech soldiers will have their first collective exercises with NATO troops in western Bosnia.

- According to a so-called "Green Report" which the Agriculture Ministry prepares every year, losses in agriculture last year of 500 to 700 million crowns can be blamed for the most part on agricultural cooperatives.
- Industry and Trade Minister Karel Kuhnl became a member of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA).

- Parliamentary Chairman and Chairman of the Social Democrats (CSSD), Milos Zeman, is happy with the growing trend supporting his party. This is in reaction to a survey from Median, according to which 16.8 percent of Czechs want Zeman for prime minister, one percent more than Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- The leader of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL), Josef Lux, interprets the low level of trust that citizens have in parliament and the Senate as a call for a change in policy.
- Elektrotechnicke Zavody Teplice signed a contract to manufacture high-tension distributors with Siemens AG.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Bosch Diesel plans to build a factory in Jihlava for manufacturing components for freight vehicles. After Ford's announced investment of 1.6 billion crowns, it is the second largest foreign investment into Czech auto parts manufacturing.
- The director of Motoinvest, Pavel Tykac, announced yesterday that Motoinvest Group is not able to take the pressure placed on it, and the group will disband September 1.
- Skoda Plzen made its first subsidiary for air transport bankrupt. In the last few months, Skoda Air was sinking due to large debts.
- Agriculture Minister Josef Lux said if negative foreign-trade trends do not change, it will be necessary to return to discussions over import surcharges.
- At present, the state has a total of 12.7 billion crowns to cover flood damages, according to Deputy Finance Minister Jana Furstova.
- The largest domestic coffee maker -- Tchibo Praha -- is planning to increase its prices by up to 15 percent and its competitors should follow this step.
PRAVO - President Vaclav Havel said that if conflicts within the coalition continue, he is prepared to use his authority and intervene.
- According to an analysis from J.P. Morgan, while unemployment should decrease in Hungary, Poland and Slovakia, it should increase in the Czech Republic.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Komercni Banka bought up cabinet flood bonds worth 100 million crowns from the first wave. It will begin offering them from August 1 at face values of 1,000 and 10,000 crowns. Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka also has the same amount.

- The chairman of the Social Democrats (CSSD), Milos Zeman, backs Josef Lux, chairman of the Christian Democrats (KDU-CSL) on both points of the coalition conflict from the end of last week. He is in favour of selling tanks to Algeria and disapproves of privatising IPB at a low price.
